ack.subject: We received your application — {role}
ack.body:
Hi {name},

Thanks for applying for {role} — we've received your application and a recruiter will review it shortly. We'll be in touch about the next steps.

Best,
{team}

rejection.subject: Your application — {role}
rejection.opening:
Hi {name},

Thank you for your interest in {role} and for the time you put into your application. After careful review, we won't be moving forward at this stage.
rejection.early: This is not a reflection of your potential. Early in a career the strongest signal is trajectory, and we'd genuinely encourage you to apply again as you build out more hands-on experience — we'll keep your profile on file.
rejection.standard: The decision came down to fit against the specific needs of this role right now, not a judgement of your ability. We'd welcome a future application as our teams and openings evolve, and we'll keep your profile on file.

interviewConfirmation.subject: Interview confirmed — {role}
interviewConfirmation.length: Please set aside about {minutes} minutes for the call.
interviewConfirmation.normal:
Hi {name},

Your interview for {role} is booked for {slot}.{length} We'll send a reminder before the call with everything you need.

If you need to change the time, just reply and we'll sort it out.

See you then,
{team}

interviewReminder.subject: Reminder — your interview {slot}

interviewInvite.subject: Your AI first-round screen — {role}

onboarding.subject: Welcome aboard — {role}
onboarding.body:
Hi {name},

We're delighted you're joining us as {role}! Welcome to the team.

Your onboarding is now underway. Our People team will reach out shortly with your start date, paperwork, equipment, and a first-week plan so you can hit the ground running.

We can't wait to work with you.

Warmly,
{team}

aiDisclosure.title: How this works
aiDisclosure.body: We use AI to assist screening and interviews — assessing your <highlight>skills, experience, and fit</highlight> for the role. A human reviews and makes every advance, offer, and rejection decision; nothing adverse is decided automatically. You can ask for a human review at any point.

tab.title: Match candidate → jobs
tab.intro: Run a candidate against the whole corpus. KO filters narrow it, a multi-factor scorer ranks the survivors, and the per-match reasoning explains the fit. Student / career-switcher profiles are scored on a different profile — potential replaces years of experience, skills are provenance-discounted, and the KO filter keeps only entry-eligible roles.

interviewSim.caseDescCase: Same six phases, but the mechanism probe, the counterfactual and the deliberate hint all work a shared designed case — every candidate on the role hears the same scenario, so ratings are genuinely comparable. Demo case: {case}. Each phase still produces a quotable observation for a rubric construct:
interviewSim.caseDescGeneric: The agent leads the conversation through the six-phase early-career script — concrete → mechanism → counterfactual → metacognitive — and injects one deliberate hint mid-problem to read coachability live. Every phase exists to produce a quotable observation for a rubric construct:
interviewSim.studentFooter: In the real flow this transcript is scored on the early-career BARS rubric and compared within the student cohort. The full script is documented in About → Early-career students.
interviewSim.regularDesc: The standard ungrounded quick screen: the agent asks a few short questions about recent experience with brief follow-ups, under {min} minutes. In the real flow the transcript is scored on the five experienced-hire axes.

students.exampleIntro: Three illustrative students against one junior backend role. Each carries a bounded, evidence-driven weighting — the axes are the same, how much each counts is earned. The real version of this table lives in Decisions → Group evaluation.
students.caseBadgeTitle: Fed by the case-grounded phases — these ratings gate observed minting
students.scoringFootnote: Hover a rating for the verbatim evidence behind it — no quote, no score. Adéla's case-tagged constructs average 4.3 on quoted evidence — above the 4/5 minting bar, so her case-grounded interview itself minted the observed skills that narrow her band. Bára outscores her on potential but stays wide until something is observed; Cyril's fluent delivery is scored separately from the content of his reasoning (and his 2s on the case constructs mean nothing is minted).
students.scriptIntro: The thought-script the agent follows (~{min} minutes), shown in its case-designed form. The skeleton is fixed — concrete → mechanism → counterfactual → metacognitive — and the agent may improvise follow-ups, but the highlighted phases draw their questions from the role's designed case, so every candidate works the same material. Hints are injected on purpose: coachability only exists live.
students.scriptFootnote: Every rating must cite a verbatim transcript quote (no quote, no score), a short or evasive answer widens the confidence band instead of lowering the score, and reasoning content is scored separately from delivery fluency — nerves and non-native English are not weak thinking. When the case-fed constructs all rate on quoted evidence and average above bar, the interview itself mints observed-provenance skills onto the candidate's profile.
